title: AI Images
subtitle: Create and edit images with intent: memes, photo edits, logos, marketing graphics and study aids — using the vocabulary designers use.
bigIdea: Image AI starts from random noise and 'denoises' it step by step toward what your prompt describes. The more precisely you use design language — subject, composition, style, lighting, format — the more control you have. Great images come from design decisions, not lucky prompts.
objectives: Explain how a diffusion model turns noise into an image, and why prompts and reference images change the result.
Write image prompts with the Image Prompt Formula (Subject · Setting · Style · Composition · Lighting · Format) using professional terms like shot type, angle and aspect ratio.
Edit images ethically with AI tools (background removal, generative fill, inpainting/outpainting, upscaling) and label edits honestly.
Design an original brand identity (logo, colors, fonts) and marketing graphics using visual hierarchy and a clear call to action.
Create accurate study aids (flashcards, diagrams, visual notes) and fact-check AI-generated text and details in images.

vocabulary.definition: An image AI that starts with random static and cleans it up step by step into a picture.
vocabulary.analogy: A sculptor chipping a statue out of a block of marble.
vocabulary.example: Nano Banana, ChatGPT Images, Firefly.

vocabulary.definition: Random dots/static an image AI starts from.
vocabulary.analogy: TV static or a foggy window.
vocabulary.example: Step 1 of every diffusion image.

vocabulary.definition: Making a new image from a written prompt.
vocabulary.analogy: Describing a picture to an artist on the phone.
vocabulary.example: 'A pixel-art fox astronaut'.

vocabulary.definition: Giving the AI a picture to guide the new one.
vocabulary.analogy: Showing your hairdresser a photo.
vocabulary.example: Upload a sketch, get a polished version.

vocabulary.definition: The shape of an image: width compared to height.
vocabulary.analogy: Phone screen vs. TV screen.
vocabulary.example: 1:1 square post, 9:16 story, 16:9 slide.

vocabulary.definition: How things are arranged in the picture.
vocabulary.analogy: Arranging furniture in a room.
vocabulary.example: Subject on the left third, empty space for text.

vocabulary.definition: Imagine a 3×3 grid; put important things on the lines or where they cross.
vocabulary.analogy: Tic-tac-toe board over your photo.
vocabulary.example: Horizon on the bottom line.

vocabulary.definition: How close and from where the 'camera' sees the subject.
vocabulary.analogy: Standing far away vs. right up close.
vocabulary.example: Close-up, wide shot, bird's-eye view, low angle.

vocabulary.definition: The artistic look of an image.
vocabulary.analogy: The same song played as rock or as jazz.
vocabulary.example: Pixel art, watercolor, 3D clay, flat vector.

vocabulary.definition: Changing or filling a selected part INSIDE an image.
vocabulary.analogy: Patching a hole in jeans.
vocabulary.example: Replace the plain mug on the desk with a plant.

vocabulary.definition: Extending an image beyond its edges.
vocabulary.analogy: Drawing what's outside a window frame.
vocabulary.example: Turn a square photo into a wide banner.

vocabulary.definition: Making an image bigger and sharper with AI.
vocabulary.analogy: A magnifying glass that also adds detail.
vocabulary.example: Turn a small logo into a poster-size file.

vocabulary.definition: A brand's symbol; wordmark = styled name, icon = picture symbol.
vocabulary.analogy: A team's jersey crest.
vocabulary.example: Combination mark: icon + name.

vocabulary.definition: The set of colors, fonts, logo and style a brand always uses.
vocabulary.analogy: A school uniform for a company.
vocabulary.example: Brand board with 3 colors, 2 fonts, logo.

vocabulary.definition: Making the most important thing the most noticeable.
vocabulary.analogy: Headlines are bigger than the article text.
vocabulary.example: Big product photo → headline → small details.

vocabulary.definition: The words telling viewers what to do next.
vocabulary.analogy: A 'Press here' sign on a button.
vocabulary.example: 'Try it free', 'Shop now'.

vocabulary.definition: Difference between light/dark or colors that makes things stand out.
vocabulary.analogy: White chalk on a dark board.
vocabulary.example: Yellow text on dark blue.

vocabulary.definition: Hidden or visible labels showing an image was AI-made or edited.
vocabulary.analogy: A signature on a painting.
vocabulary.example: SynthID, C2PA 'Content Credentials', #MadeWithAI.

vocabulary.definition: A familiar image format people reuse with new captions.
vocabulary.analogy: A joke format like 'knock knock'.
vocabulary.example: Two-panel 'expectation vs. reality'.

vocabulary.definition: Learning with words AND pictures together.
vocabulary.analogy: Two roads to the same memory.
vocabulary.example: Flashcard with a term + a drawing.

gamification.questLine: A fictional startup (chosen by each student) hires the Guild to build its visual identity: memes for buzz, edited product shots, a logo, marketing graphics and study aids for its customers.
gamification.badge: 🎨 Pixel Forger — awarded for a complete Brand Kit that scores 3+ on every rubric row.
gamification.boss: Brand Kit Showcase: logo + brand board + 1 social post + 1 poster + 1 study aid, all disclosed as AI-assisted, presented in a 60-second pitch.
sideQuests: Style Remix: recreate one of your images in 5 different art styles and name each one correctly (+25 XP).
Hands & Text Hunt: find 3 typical AI image glitches (extra fingers, garbled text, impossible shadows) in your own outputs and fix them (+25 XP).
Make a 'How AI images work' comic strip for younger students (+25 XP).
Manual vs. AI: do the same edit by hand in Photopea and with AI; write which was better and why (+25 XP).

safety.teach: Gemini (school) is the default; under-18 Gemini accounts can't edit uploads, so photo editing uses Canva/Adobe Express for Education. Higgsfield is 18+ → teacher demo only; ChatGPT Images 13+ with permission.
Photo edits only on objects, stock/public-domain images, or AI-generated characters. Never classmates, teachers or celebrities. Discuss: how could an edited photo hurt someone?
No real brand logos, celebrities or copyrighted characters in prompts ('in the style of [living artist]' is also off-limits — describe the style instead). Our brands are fictional and original.
Every image gets a #MadeWithAI or 'AI-edited' label. Marketing must not show fake product results or fake reviews.
AI diagrams and flashcards can contain wrong labels or garbled text. Every study aid is checked against a textbook before it's shared.
Memes punch at situations, not people. No memes about classmates, groups or real people.

finalProject.title: Brand Kit for a Fictional Startup
finalProject.brief: Each student invents a startup (e.g. eco water bottles, a dog-walking app, a bakery for robots). Using AI image tools and Canva, they produce a complete Brand Kit and pitch it to the class in 60 seconds. The brand carries forward into the Video and Website modules.
deliverables: Brand Brief (name, audience, 3 personality words, mission sentence)
Logo (combination mark) + icon-only version, tested at small size
Brand board: 3–5 colors with hex codes, 2 fonts, logo, mood images
1 social media post (1:1 or 9:16) with headline and CTA
1 study aid for customers (how-to diagram or flashcard set) that is fact-checked
Prompt Log with at least 3 iterations per asset and disclosure labels

levels: Assets don't match each other or the audience
Consistent brand that fits the audience and personality words
Every choice (color, font, style) is explained with design vocabulary
Image Prompt Formula used; 3+ logged iterations per asset
Advanced control: reference images, shot types, aspect ratios, targeted edits
Clear hierarchy, readable text, strong CTA
Persuasive and honest; tested with a classmate and improved
Uses real brands/people or no disclosure
All assets original, disclosed, study aid fact-checked
Explains how they avoided bias, copyright and misleading claims

finalProject.levelUp: Create a consistent mascot character for the brand and place it in 3 different scenes (consistency challenge), plus an animated sticker or GIF version to bridge into the Video module.

support: Image Prompt Formula fill-in card with word banks (styles, shots, lighting).
Brand Brief template with example answers; choose from 6 starter startup ideas.
Canva templates pre-selected and shared with the class.
Pair-programming style roles: Prompter and Art Director, swapping each asset.
Reduce the kit to logo + 1 post + 1 study aid if needed (still eligible for the badge at 'Proficient').
extension: Use reference images and describe a consistent mascot across scenes.
Write a mini brand style guide (do's and don'ts).
Compare two generators for the same prompt and write a tool review with evidence.
Explore color theory: complementary vs. analogous palettes; test contrast for accessibility (WCAG contrast checker).

carryForward: The startup and Brand Kit become the client for Module 2 (launch video) and Module 3 (landing page + store).
